subject: Request: legal redline / exception for Clearsight Health DPA terms
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Cc: m.garcia@clearsight.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T11:12:00-04:00
Subject: Request: legal redline / exception for Clearsight Health DPA terms

Hi team,

Clearsight Health sent back a redline of our DPA (attached) and a request for a narrow exception. High-level asks: they want to add their EU analytics provider (listed in the attached CSV) as a subprocessor, shorten telemetry retention from our standard 365 days to 90 days for signal-level telemetry, and allow limited, aggregated use of anonymized telemetry for model improvement (explicitly excluding patient-identifiable content).

Legal received this under enterprise procurement (deal DL-8792). Given the regulated nature of their data, I need Product and Security to review the operational and risk implications. Specific asks:
- Product (Dev): can we implement a tenant-scoped retention override (90 days) that applies to telemetry/metrics but preserves audit logs for compliance as required? Will this affect caching (KV cache) or routing behavior? Estimate dev effort and rollout risk.
- Security (Kimberly): do we have the controls to accept the named subprocessor for EU processing? What additional evidence (AICPA SOC2, EU data residency confirmation, subprocessor agreements) do you need?

Attachments: Clearsight_DPA_redline_v3.pdf, clearsight_subprocessors_20270410.csv

Can each of you reply with a short assessment and whether you can sign off on a scoped exception (if mitigations applied) by EOD Thu (2027-04-15)? They are asking to close this quickly to complete procurement.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: dev.patel@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, m.garcia@clearsight.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T14:08:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: legal redline / exception for Clearsight Health DPA terms

Thanks Lauren — quick technical questions to scope work: 

1) When you say "telemetry/metrics" retention to 90 days, does Clearsight mean: request/response traces, request headers, token-level logs, and model telemetry (prompt/response embeddings)? Or do they only mean system-level metrics (latency, error rates)? The distinction matters for KV cache and cost.
2) Do we need to ensure that their telemetry stays in an EU region (data residency)? We have per-region routing but need to confirm that the analytics subprocessor will also be EU-based.
3) For the "anonymized model improvement" clause: are we allowed to perform aggregation and training on derived features (embeddings)? If so, are we expected to exclude any records flagged as PHI/patient-identifiable?

Operational constraints: we can add a tenant-scoped retention override that applies to persisted telemetry buckets and metrics indexing (90 days) without touching real-time KV cache eviction (KV cache is ephemeral and generally kept for short sessions). The trickiness is "model improvement" — our model training pipeline ingests telemetry in a separate, audited workspace; we'd need a filter to exclude any data marked by Clearsight as PHI and a signed attestation that they will not include patient content in the feed. Estimated engineering effort: 1.5 engineer-months for the filtering / tenant config and 2-3 weeks for QA and rollout if prioritized.

If Product can do the config and add a gating flag to prevent telemetry from reaching the training pipeline unless cleared, I can support a scoped exception. Need Security to confirm subprocessor risk.

- Dev Patel
Senior Product Engineer, Runtime
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: m.garcia@clearsight.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T16:35:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: legal redline / exception for Clearsight Health DPA terms

Lauren / team — thanks for the summary. Initial Security view: potential path but requires evidence and mitigations. Needs: 

1) Subprocessor evidence: For each named vendor in clearsight_subprocessors_20270410.csv we need SOC2 Type II (or ISO 27001) and confirmation of EU data residency or adequate SCCs + local contractual commitments. We also need Clearsight to sign our subprocessor addendum if they intend to pass data to a third party.
2) Telemetry scope: we need clarity on whether request/response pairs or any PII-containing text will be included. If model improvement uses prompt/response content (even anonymized), it's higher risk. 
3) KV cache and model memory: product says KV cache is ephemeral — we still need to ensure retention settings do not inadvertently persist cache snapshots or debug logs.

Mitigations I want before sign-off:
- Documentation from Clearsight confirming they will remove/flag PHI and that data used for model improvement will be pre-filtered and hashed.
- A Data Processing Addendum clause that excludes patient-identifiable content from training datasets, with auditability.
- Vendor evidence (SOC2 or equivalent) for the analytics subprocessor.

If Product can add the gating flag Dev mentioned and we get the vendor evidence and the DPA language tightened, Security would be open to signing a scoped exception limited to 90 days with quarterly review.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security Compliance
From: m.garcia@clearsight.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-12T09:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Request: legal redline / exception for Clearsight Health DPA terms

Hi Lauren / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our analytics partner (MedSignal EU) is EU-based; I attached their SOC2 reference and contact in the vendor CSV. We are happy to sign Redwood's subprocessor addendum.
- On retention: we can accept 90 days for telemetry, but 180 days would be more operationally useful for our fraud detection cadence. Would Redwood consider 180 days?
- On model improvement: we will only provide fully pseudonymized aggregates and will explicitly exclude patient-identifiable text. We can provide an attestation and a sample transform pipeline.

We can expedite the vendor docs into DocuSign (link below) if that helps. We are on a tight procurement timeline and would appreciate an interim, scoped approval while we complete vendor evidence collection.

Regards,
Maria Garcia
VP Legal & Ops, Clearsight Health
Attachments: MedSignal_SOC2_summary.pdf
Links: https://legal.clearsight.ai/dpa-redline/CL-452
From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: m.garcia@clearsight.ai
Date: 2027-04-13T09:47:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: legal redline / exception for Clearsight Health DPA terms — proposed path forward

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps so Legal has a record: 

Summary:
- Clearsight requests subprocessor addition (MedSignal EU) + retention window reduction for telemetry.
- Product can implement a tenant-scoped retention override (90 days) and a gating flag to prevent telemetry from entering the model-training pipeline without explicit opt-in. Estimated delivery: feature branch + QA ~3 weeks if prioritized.
- Security requires SOC2/ISO evidence from MedSignal and an attestation from Clearsight that they will exclude PHI from any data used for model improvement.

Proposed path forward (ask to Security/Product):
1) Product (Dev) to create a short runbook and a minimal acceptance test for the gating flag and retention override by 2027-04-20. Please flag any blockers by EOD 2027-04-15.
2) Security (Kimberly) to confirm whether the provided MedSignal SOC2 summary is sufficient or list additional required evidence by 2027-04-14.
3) Legal (Lauren) to prepare a scoped DPA amendment limiting allowed processing for model improvement to pseudonymized aggregates and requiring quarterly review.
4) If Product and Security sign off on the mitigations, Legal will issue a 90-day scoped exception to allow procurement to proceed while we collect final vendor evidence.

I'll act as approver to coordinate internal signoffs. If either Product or Security cannot meet the deadlines, notify Lauren and I and we'll escalate to the CTO/GC.

Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
